themes.title: G42 weighs selling majority control for chip access
themes.summary: Bloomberg reports Abu Dhabi's G42 is weighing selling a majority stake to US investors to lock in secure AI chip supply. The potential deal shows compute access has become a strategic-asset question for Gulf sovereign champions, with equity rather than contracts emerging as the price of chip security.
themes.angle: Sovereign AI's endgame: when the crown jewel has to cede control for compute.

themes.title: Saudi Arabia becomes the US AI data-center escape hatch
themes.summary: American AI players are routing capacity to Saudi Arabia as US backlash over data centers grows: AWS is committing $5.3 billion and 50MW to a Saudi AI Zone by 2028, Together AI is eyeing Saudi capacity, and a US firm is building a 250MW data centre there. The Kingdom is monetizing power, permits and policy at a moment of American NIMBYism.
themes.angle: KSA is profiting from America's data-center conflict.

themes.title: Frontier agent economics reset: Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra
themes.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5.1 made agents cheaper and launched with fewer interruptions, while OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can stay on a job and use a computer — both within days of each other. The competitive battleground has shifted from benchmarks to the cost and reliability of long-running agents.
themes.angle: Agent economics, not scores, is the new frontier war.

themes.title: GCC enterprise AI: Aramco, Adobe, DIFC push forward
themes.summary: Gulf enterprises are buying AI capability at state scale: Saudi Aramco signed up to $3.7 billion in potential deals with French firms including AI technology, Adobe is offering free AI tools in Saudi Arabia as part of a $4 billion expansion, and DIFC's Innovation Hub widened its Global South reach. Vendors are pricing accordingly.
themes.angle: Gulf enterprises buy AI at national scale; vendors price for it.

themes.title: The humanoid era: OpenAI, Skild, and Gulf fleet deals
themes.summary: Altman says OpenAI will build humanoids, extending its ambition beyond software; Skild's S1 promises to cut robot training to a single video; and Dubai-based No Competition signed a five-year deal for up to 10,000 humanoid robots annually. Physical AI is moving from demo to procurement.
themes.angle: The Gulf is buying the humanoid future at fleet scale.

themes.title: AI macro: servers surge, gadgets get pricier
themes.summary: The AI buildout is showing up in hard numbers: Hon Hai's monthly sales climbed 52% on AI server demand, TCS is committing ~$7.4 billion for a one-gigawatt data center campus in India, and the FT reports the AI boom has ended the era of ever-cheaper electronics.
themes.angle: AI is an inflation and capex story, not just a software story.

themes.title: China turns AI tokens into a consumer economy
themes.summary: Chinese banks and carriers have turned AI tokens into rewards, monthly plans and even collateral, while commentators argue Chinese open-source models are becoming the global baseline or 'metric system' for AI. It is a different commercialization path from the US subscription model.
themes.angle: China treats AI usage like mobile data, not software licenses.

themes.title: AI policy and safety stack up: pause calls, agent rules, surveillance revolt
themes.summary: Policy and safety moves accumulated: OpenAI pledged new rules for reporting troubling AI-agent behavior, Sanders took his global AI pause proposal to Fox News with enforcement questions open, and US Republicans are revolting against Flock's AI-powered licence-plate surveillance. The politics of AI are fragmenting across left and right.
themes.angle: AI governance is becoming a cross-aisle, cross-border scramble.
